summary: R1_S1 reports, in an abstract-only metadynamics study of sticker-spacer condensates, kinetic arrest when stickers exchange slowly, while faster exchange can allow merger toward equilibrium; this supports the general possibility of exchange-limited arrest, not transcription-generated internal cavities in this RNA system. R1_S3 reports gel-like kinetic trapping for percolated beta-sheet networks in proteins with multiple LARKS, a material-specific route. R1_S2 is a review noting condensates can retard diffusion; R1_S4 concerns electrostatics and phase-behavior modeling. All are abstract-level background. E1 motion summaries show B n=279, median final squared displacement 1.596 um^2 over median 98 frames, with top-100 high-displacement median 123.05 um^2; A n=838, median 0.636 um^2 over 159 frames, top-100 median 19.58 um^2. Unequal track durations and selected upper tails make these summaries insufficient to infer arrested cavity motion. I retain C1 as an unconfirmed hypothesis, sharpened to slow exchange/percolation of reversible RNA loop junctions as a possible memory mechanism. Its conditional threshold consequence remains x_ss=alpha*r*tau>x_c for constant r. No target-specific confirmation or DNA-to-RNA concentration inference is made.

candidates.target: Delayed emergence and persistence of internal RNA-poor cavity area in transcribing RNA droplets, especially the B/A contrast.
known_relations: E0: mean segmented area fraction is similar at t=0 (A .01487, B .01381); at 24 h A .00446 and B .08918. These are pooled-field image measures, not independent preparation-level inference.

R1_S1 (abstract only; 2024-12-15) describes slow sticker exchange causing kinetic arrest in simulated sticker-spacer condensate coalescence; faster exchange at similar saturation permits merger to equilibrium. It does not study transcription-produced cavities or this RNA nanostructure.

R1_S3 (abstract only; 2023-06-29) describes kinetically trapped gel-like condensates for proteins with at least two LARKS through percolated beta-sheet networks; protein-specific chemistry and topology limit transfer.

R1_S2 is a review abstract on condensate tradeoffs including diffusion retardation; R1_S4 is about electrostatics and model phase-behavior accuracy in charge-rich condensates. Neither directly supplies the missing cavity mechanism.

E1 is existing preparation-1 tracking summary: B has fewer and shorter tracks than A, but a much larger selected top-100 displacement summary. Track-level censoring/distribution and cavity size/identity are unavailable in the summary.
hypotheses: H1 (new, unconfirmed): production of associative RNA creates a percolating population of loop-mediated junctions whose exchange is slow relative to production and stress relaxation; a threshold crossing traps solvent-rich internal domains. This combines known general arrest possibilities with a new, unverified bridge to the target RNA and cavity formation.

H1a (mechanistic bridge hypothesis): self-complementary terminal RNA loops act as stickers; slow junction exchange plus sufficient network connectivity can produce a long-lived arrested state. No supplied source establishes these assumptions for this material.
H2 alternative: amplification-linked composition/product heterogeneity changes equilibrium phase coexistence; at matched final composition after equilibration, schedule history should not matter.
H3 alternative: reaction carryover or measurement/segmentation differences associated with amplification explain some or all of the condition contrast.

gaps.description: Do reversible RNA loop junctions have exchange/connectivity conditions capable of arresting this network, and can production rate cross a threshold that traps internal cavities? R1 supports generic exchange-limited arrest only in other condensate systems.
Causal effects of amplification on template/product heterogeneity versus reaction carryover remain unresolved.
Tracking summaries do not resolve cavity-specific mobility, coarsening, or arrest because durations and selected displacement summaries differ; network state and phase composition are unmeasured.

predictions: H1 predicts equal-integrated-production schedules can differ if only the faster schedule raises x above x_c; H2 predicts convergence after matched final composition and equilibration.
After threshold crossing, cavity area should persist and cavity-specific coarsening/mobility should plateau; E1 summaries cannot yet test this due to unequal track duration and selection.

Conditional 36-48 h commitment: if H1 arrest has occurred in B by 24 h, its mean segmented cavity area fraction should remain above A at 36 and 48 h, with slower growth than the 12-24 h increase. This is qualitative and may fail if the mapping changes or no arrest occurred.
checks: Units remain consistent: alpha*r and x/tau are h^-1; qdot terms are h^-1.
At r=0, x decays exponentially with tau; if x remains below x_c, the model creates no new cavities.
The generic literature relation is about condensate coalescence or protein-network aging, not RNA cavity nucleation; the bridge is a marked hypothesis.
The post-threshold freeze rule builds persistence into the model and needs independent cavity-specific motion/coarsening evidence.
E1 is not interpreted as proof of arrest: B track durations are shorter and high-displacement tail summary differs markedly.
evidence_conflicts: E0 is compatible with delayed B cavity emergence but cannot identify mechanism or causal effect.
